text:
Agent: Thank you for calling card services, this is Rachel. How can I help you today?
Customer: Hi, my debit card got declined at the grocery store, and I know there's money in the account. I was really embarrassed.
Agent: I'm so sorry about that. Let me take a look. Can I have your name and the last four digits of the card?
Customer: Tom Bradley, and it's, uh, two-six-one-one.
Agent: Thank you, Mr. Bradley. I see that our fraud system flagged a transaction this morning, a purchase of nine hundred and forty dollars at an electronics store in another state, and it placed a temporary block on your card.
Customer: That wasn't me. I haven't left town.
Agent: I figured. Let's confirm. Did you make any purchase at that store?
Customer: No, absolutely not.
Agent: Okay, I'll mark that charge as fraud, cancel this card and issue a new one. You'll get it in three to five business days, and you'll receive a provisional credit for the fraudulent charge.
Customer: And what do I do in the meantime? I have bills.
Agent: You can add the digital card to your phone wallet right now and use it for contactless payments. I can send a link.
Customer: That would help a lot. Thanks.
Agent: Of course. Is there anything else I can help with?
Customer: No, that's it.

metadata.note: customer calls about a declined card and fraud alert
